fixes.find: City & Suburban installs American Standard heat pump equipment. It also sets the outdoor temperature at which a backup heat source takes over. A written proposal should specify the outdoor temperature at which a backup heat source takes over, so the house stays warm through a deep cold snap. fixes.find: Not by itself. A heat pump moves heat rather than burning fuel, so it is efficient in most Chicago weather.
fixes.replace: It depends on model performance, utility rates, the heat loss of the building and how much the backup runs. A heat pump moves heat rather than burning fuel, so it can be efficient in much Chicago weather, but efficiency alone does not guarantee a lower bill.
fixes.why: MAJOR: 'Not by itself' implies cheaper bill; lead with what running cost depends on

fixes.find: City & Suburban sets the thermostat changeover on either arrangement.
fixes.replace: A useful comparison asks for the expected changeover temperature, the backup type and local gas and electric rates, rather than a promised saving.

fixes.find: A straightforward changeover usually runs one to two days. It runs longer when electrical work or duct changes are part of the scope. Crews recover refrigerant from the old system, then set the new outdoor unit clear of snow drift.

fixes.find: Burning smells, smoke, repeated breaker trips, or a cabinet encased in ice are reasons to shut the system off at the disconnect.
fixes.replace: Smoke, sparks or a burning smell means leaving the building and calling 911 from outside. Repeated breaker trips or a cabinet encased in ice call for service: leave the breaker off, keep clear of the iced unit, and set the thermostat to off if that is safe.
fixes.why: CRITICAL: smoke/burning grouped with shutting off at the outdoor disconnect; separate fire evacuation from ice/breaker service calls
